summary: M1 fifth run: T66 (CI mutation split across a matrix of parallel jobs, Sylvester 1 October) and T69 (composer validate --strict), then the exit criteria of the whole block. Exit criteria E11, E12, E14 and E16 failed in the fourth run; E15 fails only on wording and counts as passed.

tasks.title: main green on GitHub CI within the 15-minute budget
tasks.goal: Sylvester decided 1 October how CI runs mutation on changed files: (2) split the mutation steps across a GitHub Actions matrix of parallel jobs, so the run time is the slowest job's, parallelizing rather than cutting (GUARDRAILS 10, 7.3); and (1) the main session pushes to main after each merged task, so a CI run on main usually mutates one task. Branch wip/M1-T66 (183f1e1, worktree ~/Projects/Cbox/cms-worktrees/M1-T66) holds the earlier attempt, committed and with composer check green: it fixed the false kills (a load-time warning in InvariantCoverageTest made every mutation count as caught), the MarkersTest race, the memory limit, made the Arch layer rule fast (137 s to 19 s), ran each mutation with only the test files its filter can select, covered constants, enum cases, properties and attributes, ran the Postgres step only on the mutations the fast suites missed, turned PCOV off for mutation processes, ran Pint in parallel, and added tests that brought the seeding classes, the kernel command codecs and RestRequest to 80 %. Rebase it on main and keep all of that. Then add the matrix: bin/ci and ci.yml split mutation on changed files into N shards by file (deterministic, every changed file in exactly one shard, the fast suites' step and the Postgres step per shard), a job per shard in parallel with the other gates in their own job, and a final job that fails unless every shard and gate passed and that merges the shards' reports into one verdict per class (80 % over all its mutations). The shard count comes from the number of changed files, with a maximum, and each shard's wall time stays within the 15-minute budget for a block-sized diff (the whole of M1 since 59f0d88: 966 files, about 25,000 mutations). The containerized run (compose.ci.yaml) runs the same shards locally. Classes still below 80 % after the shards run get tests that kill their surviving mutations; a mutation that no test can kill in practice is reported under "Til review af Sylvester" with the class and the mutation, never excluded and never by lowering the threshold. Record each shard's wall time and the total in PROGRESS.md.
acceptance: A CI run on main with CMS_CI_BASE_REF=59f0d88 passes with every shard within 15 minutes (record the times); the containerized run of the same shards passes
Every changed file of the diff is mutated in exactly one shard, shown by a test of the sharding with planted file lists
The final job fails when any shard or gate fails or a class is below 80 % over its mutations in all shards, shown by a test
The work of 183f1e1 is on main: the false-kill fix with its guard test, the faster Arch layer rule with its equivalence test, the mutation test-file selection and the new tests
composer check, composer check:selftest and the containerized CI run are green

tasks.title: composer validate --strict passes
tasks.goal: M1 exit criterion E12 runs composer validate --strict, which fails because composer.json requires inertiajs/inertia-laravel at the exact version 3.4.0 (M1-T40). Give it a constraint Composer accepts in strict mode that keeps the tested version (such as ^3.4 with the lock unchanged at 3.4.0, or the narrowest caret or tilde range that still excludes untested majors), and make every other warning --strict reports go away the same way, without changing what the lock installs.
acceptance: composer.lock installs the same versions as before (git diff composer.lock shows only the content hash, or nothing)

blockers: M0-T47 (open under 'Til review af Sylvester'): whether the testkit's shared contract suites are left out of mutation on changed files. They live in src and get mutated, although no test can catch a mutated assertion. M1 adds several new shared suites (identity, type catalog, fragment store, CDN driver, telemetry), so E11 may fail only on them. The plan keeps them in scope as today. If E11 fails only on shared-suite assertions, the main session records it for Sylvester and does not weaken the gate.

Outward-facing names that M1 introduces beyond what the PRD fixes. These are error codes beyond the PRD's (T10), REST paths other than /v1/resolve (T38), CLI command names and the configuration key for the CLI's service credential (T39), MCP tool names (T41), the addon manifest's file name and keys (T44), the fixture addon's namespace (T45), and the exact holder line in LICENSE (T7; MIT itself is fixed by the PRD). The tasks name them after the PRD's wording and list them under 'Til review af Sylvester'. This does not block M1.

Gate 11 (review by someone other than the author) needs branch protection with required reviews on main in github.com/cboxdk/cms. That is a repository setting for Sylvester. T2 only corrects the reason; the gate stays reported as not run.

Possible: cboxdk/laravel-operations may not install on PHP 8.5 and Laravel 13. T57 checks it without changing the package. If it fails, the need goes under 'Til review af Sylvester' (GUARDRAILS 3), and T46 and T47 run their chunk actions from a console command under a recorded interpretation, so E5 and E7 do not depend on it.

Not blocking, for awareness: in M1, service credentials, actors, grants, roles, sites, nodes and routes are created only by testkit fixtures, because token issuance, login, grant commands and node commands are B1 and B2 by the build order. Real CDN drivers are B4, replica routing by consistency token is B4 and B5, planned transitions are B3, and upcasters are B3. The tasks record these as interpretations, not as decisions for Sylvester.
